_status: UNVERIFIED auditor claims. The adversarial verification pass and the synthesis/proposal agent both died on a session limit, so nothing here survived refutation. One (force_pad) was checked by hand and holds.
_method: 7 agents read each artifact's source against its own @identity 'emerges:' claim; defect classes D1 channel-misuse, D2 no-opening-state, D3 illegible-scale, D4 margin-not-shown.

findings.claim: different grammars can achieve the same goal (space-filling) through different strategies
findings.mechanism: The finding lives in the primary channel (geometry) and the supporting channels reinforce it rather than compete. `_draw_curve` (lines 167-172) normalises every curve to the SAME 488x488 px box — `scale_factor := float(draw_size) / range_max` with centring offsets — so all three panels are literally the same square filled edge to edge; that is the "same coverage" half of the claim rendered as an equality of areas. The "different strategies" half is carried by three genuinely different, correct grammars, all at densities that reach saturation: Hilbert (line 70, 4 iterations) = 255 F-moves on a 16x16 lattice, Peano (line 73, 3 iterations) = 728 F-moves on 27x27, Moore (line 76, 3 iterations) = 255 F-moves as a closed loop on 16x16 — visibly a quadrant recursion, a 9-fold sweep, and a loop that returns to its start. Colour is NOT spent on an inert variable: HILBERT_COLOR cyan / PEANO_COLOR magenta / MOORE_COLOR yellow (lines 25-27) key each panel to its grammar and the same array is reused for `label.modulate` (line 226), so name and pattern are colour-bound. Legibility holds: 3-px lines (LINE_THICKNESS, line 29) against BG_COLOR (0.04,0.04,0.06) with `emission_texture` at 0.6 energy (lines 55, 81); line spacing is 32 px (Hilbert/Moore) and 19 px (Peano), so no panel collapses into a solid block; floor labels are font_size 64 x pixel_size 0.003 = 0.19 m glyph height (lines 224-225), un-mirrored under `rotation_degrees.x = -90` and centred per panel at x = -1.067/0/+1.067 (line 229). Caveat, not a defect: `Image.create(..., false, ...)` (line 61, mipmaps off) plus `TEXTURE_FILTER_NEAREST` (line 51) will alias the 19-px-spaced Peano panel at the far end of a 3.2 m floor quad; the three-way comparison still reads grossly, so this does not block the claim.

findings.claim: the middle is not excluded — a third truth value occupies the gap (in-file wording: the discomfort of undecidable propositions — some P genuinely cannot be decided)
findings.mechanism: Nothing ever occupies the gap, and the intuitionistic case is never rendered — only asserted in 1.2 cm text. The scene contains exactly two meshes: `_true_sphere` at Vector3(-0.2, 0, 0), albedo (0.2,0.8,0.3) green (lines 33-44) and `_false_sphere` at Vector3(0.2, 0, 0), albedo (0.8,0.2,0.2) red (lines 54-65). The midpoint x=0 is occupied by a Label3D reading "∨" (lines 75-80) — the classical disjunction operator, i.e. the very thing Brouwer rejects — so the gap renders classical logic, not a third value. There is no third mesh, no third colour, no partial/undecided state anywhere in the file. The critical_parameter is `show_rejection`, and `_on_rejection_changed` (lines 108-113) does exactly one thing: `_label.queue_free()` then `_create_label()`. Both spheres keep identical positions, albedo and emission in both modes, so moving the REJECTION slider from 0 to 1 changes zero pixels of geometry. The whole difference between classical acceptance and intuitionistic doubt is two lines of `_label` text at font_size 12 x pixel_size 0.001 = 1.2 cm glyph height, default white modulate, parked at Vector3(0, -0.25, 0) below the spheres (lines 84-91) — a channel a standing visitor reads last, if at all, and only from ~40 cm away. Someone walking up sees the happy path of two-valued logic: P glowing green, ¬P glowing red, OR between them. The foreclosure the artifact exists to show — that some P falls in neither box — has no visual existence. (Compounding D1: the two most-read channels, presence and colour, are locked to a constant while the varying quantity is left to 12 pt text.)
findings.fix_sketch: Give the gap a body: add a third mesh at Vector3(0,0,0) — e.g. a grey/desaturated sphere, alpha ~0.5, slowly pulsing — created in `_create_spheres` and driven by `show_rejection` in `_on_rejection_changed`. When rejection is ON, make it visible and drop `mat1.emission`/`mat2.emission` on P and ¬P toward black (the two poles go dim and undecided while the middle lights up); when OFF, hide it and restore the emissions, and swap the midpoint glyph from "∨" to "?". Also raise `_label` to font_size 24 x pixel_size 0.002 so the accompanying text is legible standing up.

findings.claim: superposition collapses on observation — the box shows both until looked at (in-file wording: the cat is not secretly alive or dead, it is both)
findings.mechanism: Every mesh that carries the claim is sealed inside opaque geometry, and the superposition state shows neither cat rather than both. `_create_box` (lines 49-60) builds a solid `BoxMesh` of `box_size` = Vector3(0.4, 0.3, 0.3) — a closed cube, `albedo_color = Color(0.3,0.25,0.2)`, no `transparency` set — centred on the origin, so its interior is x[-0.2,0.2], y[-0.15,0.15], z[-0.15,0.15]. All three state meshes sit inside that volume: `_superposition_glow` sphere radius 0.12 at Vector3(0,0,0) (lines 108-113), `_cat_alive` sphere radius 0.08 at Vector3(0,0,0) (lines 79-83), `_cat_dead` box 0.15x0.03x0.1 at y = -box_size.y/2 + 0.025 = -0.125 (lines 95-99). All are strictly inside the shell and depth-occluded by its front faces — the glow's TRANSPARENCY_ALPHA (line 117) does not help, it still depth-tests against the opaque box. The lid does not open the box either: `_lid_mesh` is a separate slab positioned at y = box_size.y/2 + 0.01 = 0.16 (line 67) and `tween_property(_lid_mesh, "rotation_degrees:x", -110, 0.5)` (line 182) rotates it about its OWN centre with no hinge offset, so it tilts in place above a box whose top face is still there. Nothing inside is ever seen, in any state. Second mechanism, independent of the occlusion: in `_update_display` the SUPERPOSITION branch sets `_cat_alive.visible = false` and `_cat_dead.visible = false` (lines 141-142) and shows a purple stand-in sphere instead — so even with the housing removed the box would show *neither* state, not both, contradicting the claim word for word. What survives for a visitor is `_state_label` at font_size 16 x pixel_size 0.001 = 1.6 cm glyph height (lines 132-135), whose text and `modulate` do change (purple |ψ⟩ → green/red COLLAPSED), plus the slab flip: the collapse *event* is faintly legible, the superposition itself is not.
findings.fix_sketch: Make the housing see-through and the interior populated. (1) Replace the solid `BoxMesh` with a shell — either four side quads + a floor, or keep the box and set `mat.transparency = TRANSPARENCY_ALPHA`, `albedo_color.a ≈ 0.22`, `cull_mode = CULL_FRONT` so you see through the near wall. (2) Hinge the lid: parent `_lid_mesh` to an empty Node3D at z = -box_size.z/2, y = 0.16 and tween that node, so opening actually clears the aperture. (3) In the SUPERPOSITION branch set BOTH `_cat_alive.visible = true` and `_cat_dead.visible = true` at alpha ~0.45 each with counter-phased pulses in `_process` (alive bright while dead is dim), keeping the purple glow only as a halo — then "both until looked at" is literally on screen, and `visible = false` on one of them is what the click destroys.

findings.claim: point_mode transforms the screen into a live coordinate tracker — it shows the trajectory of a grabbed point in relative space, turning a simple grab into a navigation display
findings.mechanism: The screen's dominant motion is a self-firing score/particle loop that runs while the player stands still, and the trajectory is the quietest thing on the panel. (a) `const POINT_SNAP_DIST := 0.5` (line 99) vs `_spawn_new_target()` (445-450) which draws the target from `randf_range(-0.5, 0.5)` in x and y. The tracked point rests at pos == ZERO (origin captured at 389-390), so the target lands inside snap range with probability pi*0.5^2/1^2 = 0.785 — about 4 of every 5 targets satisfy `d < POINT_SNAP_DIST` on the very frame they spawn, so 405-409 fires at once: `_point_score += 1` plus a 20-particle burst (455-464), 0.5 s explode timer (407), then 414-416 spawns another. Net result with nobody touching anything: a firework and +1 SCORE roughly every 0.5 s, forever. (b) Because the respawn at 416 happens after the hit test and the target is drawn only `if not screen_ref._point_exploding` (1299), the pulsing ring, 56 px crosshair and distance line (1303-1312) are on screen for a single frame per cycle — the whole target-drawing block is effectively dead code, and what the visitor actually sees is continuous particle motion uncorrelated with their hand. (c) The trajectory the claim names is `const MAX_TRAIL := 100` (89) appended once per frame unconditionally (394-396) — 1.1 s of history at 90 fps, and it collapses to a single dot when the point is still — drawn at width `1.0 + t * 1.5` and alpha `0.1 + t * 0.6` (1296), i.e. a <=2.5 px, <=0.7-alpha violet hairline next to a 44 px pulsing target and radius-2.5 particles. Motion and size are spent on an autonomous game variable; the grabbed point's path gets the channel nobody reads first. Note the header/grid/axes/data panel do render at t=0 (147, 1266-1348), so this is not a D2.
findings.fix_sketch: Spawn targets outside reach so the hit is earned: `randf_range` onto a ring of radius 0.8-1.6 and drop POINT_SNAP_DIST to ~0.15; require pos to have exceeded the snap radius once before the hit test at 405 can fire. Window the trail by path length instead of frames (keep samples until accumulated arc length > ~2 m, MAX_TRAIL ~400) and draw it at >=4 px with head alpha >=0.6 so the trajectory outweighs the particles.

findings.claim: the theoretical PDF curve overlays the histogram and they converge — shape is not noise, noise has shape
findings.mechanism: The two things that are supposed to converge are plotted in different vertical units, so at the defaults the curve is nowhere near the bars. Bars are peak-normalized: `height = float(_bins[i]) / float(max_count) * display_height * BAR_FILL_RATIO + BAR_HEIGHT_MIN` (line 400) — the modal bar is always 0.9*0.4 + 0.01 = 0.37 m. The curve plots raw density: `_im.surface_add_vertex(Vector3(x, y * display_height * 0.8, 0.01))` (415) with `y = _theoretical_pdf(x_norm)` (413). Default Gaussian sigma = 0.15 (line 62) gives peak pdf = 1/(0.15*sqrt(TAU)) = 2.66, so the curve peaks at 2.66 * 0.32 = 0.85 m against a panel that spans y in [-0.02, 0.42] (back panel, 157-160) — 2.3x the panel height. The curve exits the top wherever pdf > 0.42/0.32 = 1.3125, i.e. x_norm in [0.322, 0.678]: the central 36% of the width carrying 76% of the probability mass, exactly where the bars are tallest, is off-panel in empty air. Exponential default rate 3.0 (68) is worse: pdf(0) = 6 -> 1.92 m, 4.8x the panel. Poisson lambda = 5 (65) fails the other way: peak ~0.53 -> 0.17 m, under half the modal bar, and since bars are BAR_DEPTH 0.02 boxes centred at z = 0 (193, 207) while the curve sits at z = 0.01, the curve is coplanar with the bar front faces — z-fighting/buried. On top of that the curve is `Mesh.PRIMITIVE_LINE_STRIP` on an ImmediateMesh (409), a 1-px hairline with no thickness control, against 0.02 m-thick bars. In no default configuration can a visitor watch the histogram rise to meet the curve. (The startup path is fine — `_clear_samples()` at 126 calls `_update_theory_curve()`, so the curve is present from t=0; and the alpha 0.6 in color_theory is inert because `_theory_mat` never sets transparency, so it renders opaque.)
findings.fix_sketch: Normalize the curve the same way the bars are: compute pdf_max over the CURVE_SEGMENTS samples and emit `y = pdf(x)/pdf_max * display_height * BAR_FILL_RATIO` so curve peak and modal bar coincide by construction; move the vertices to z = BAR_DEPTH/2 + 0.004 so they sit in front of the bar faces instead of coplanar; and build the curve from thin quads (or chained cylinders ~0.004 m) so it has real width against the bars.

findings.claim: traffic-like lane formation where many agents converge on the same narrow corridor without coordination or negotiation
findings.mechanism: The corridor state is transient and the artifact's permanent resting state has no corridor at all; and at the two moments a corridor exists, the swarm is stalled inside a wall. (a) `if sequence_mode == 5: ... return` (FlowFieldMain.gd:43-47) sits before the timer block, so mode 5 (Perlin noise turbulence) is absorbing and the `% 6` at line 53 is unreachable once entered. Timeline from map load: mode 0 open field 0-10 s, 1 centre block 10-20, 2 U-wall 20-30, 3 zig-zag 30-40, 4 linear wind 40-50, then noise forever. Only modes 2 and 3 have corridors, so the claim is on screen for a 20 s window 20-40 s after load; every visitor arriving later, and every capture taken later, sees 200 agents drifting in a noise field with no corridor whatsoever. (b) `set_scenario()` (56) never repositions agents, and the walls get painted over wherever the swarm has just converged. After mode 0 all 200 agents sit at target (20,20) = world (0.5, 0, 0.5); mode 1 then runs `grid.fill_rect(15, 15, 10, 10, 255)` (67), covering world x,z in [-4.5, 4.5] — the swarm is now inside the wall, so integration_field = MAX_COST -> `vector_field[idx] = Vector2.ZERO` (FlowGrid.gd:114-116) -> every agent takes the wander branch (FlowAgent.gd:34-38), lerping toward a freshly random direction each frame, which averages to a stall. Same again at mode 3: agents converged on mode 2's target (20,25) = world (0.5, 0, 5.5), and `grid.fill_rect(10, 25, 30, 2, 255)` (81) covers z in [4.5, 6.5] — so the population is parked inside a wall at the exact instant the zig-zag corridor appears. Mode 2 is no better: the blob is already inside the U, 5 cells from the target, so nothing converges from across the field. (c) The gaps are not narrow anyway: wall 1 leaves x = 30..39 and wall 2 leaves x = 0..9 (79, 81) = 10 m at cell_size 1.0, and the U opening is x 12..27 = 16 m — 25-40% of the 40 m field, ~16 agent-diameters abreast (capsule radius 0.3, FlowAgent.tscn). No single-file lane can form in a gap that wide. (d) The corridor is never drawn positively: FieldVisualizer emits arrows only where `vec.length_squared() > 0.01` (FieldVisualizer.gd:27), so wall cells appear as an absence of arrows, and no collision geometry exists for them either.
findings.fix_sketch: Delete the early `return` at line 47 so the cycle keeps turning (or reorder so a corridor scenario is the resting state). Re-seed agent positions in `set_scenario()` — scatter them across the half of the field away from the target so they must actually funnel — and skip cells whose cost is 255 when placing them. Narrow the zig-zag gaps from 30-wide walls to 36-wide (3-4 cell gaps) so a lane is forced. Emit a dark quad per cost==255 cell in FieldVisualizer.update_visuals() so the corridor reads as walls rather than as missing arrows.

findings.claim: magenta dots appearing in the gap reveal that magenta is not a spectral color — it is the brain's invention to close the loop
findings.mechanism: The constraint the piece exists to show — physics only gives you 270 degrees, the spectrum cannot close itself — is never rendered; only the closed wheel is. One `smooth_t` (lines 80-81) drives both the bend, `_dots[i].position = pos_linear.lerp(pos_circle, smooth_t)` (100), and the fill, `_magenta_dots[i].scale = Vector3.ONE * smooth_t` (116). The invented segment therefore grows in at exactly the rate the arc bends, so the 90-degree gap is empty for zero frames: there is no instant at which a visitor sees a spectrum whose two ends fail to meet. Worse, the magenta dots are pinned to their final circular coordinates (112, 115) and the bottom of that arc is `sin(180)*r = 0, cos(180)*r + r = 0` -> world (0,0) — precisely where the 550 nm green dot sits in linear mode — with the gap arc only 2*0.707*1.5915 = 2.25 m wide and dot diameter 0.5 (dot_size line 17, `_create_dot` 60-62). So during the transition the magenta grows up inside the still-linear spectrum's green midsection, not in a visible void. And once settled (smooth_t = 1 for phase 0.6-1.0, i.e. 7.2 s of every 12 s cycle) nothing distinguishes the invented 90 degrees: identical dot_size, identical unshaded material, and the ramp `Color(1,0,0).lerp(Color(0.5,0,1), t)` (52) joins the spectral ends seamlessly — magenta t=0 = (1,0,0) meets `_wavelength_to_color(700)` = (1,0,0), magenta t=1 = (0.5,0,1) meets `_wavelength_to_color(400)` = (0.667,0,1). The visitor's steady-state view is an ordinary continuous colour wheel, and the identity's own `needs:` line admits `Label3D [missing]` and `wavelength labels [missing]`, so no text carries the distinction either. The only surviving cue is that magenta dots scale in place while spectral dots slide — a 2.4 s motion difference asked to carry the entire argument.
findings.fix_sketch: Decouple the two timings: keep the bend on `clamp((phase - 0.4) * 5.0, 0, 1)`, hold the closed-but-empty 270-degree arc for ~1.5 s, then ramp magenta on a delayed curve such as `clamp((phase - 0.62) * 8.0, 0, 1)` so the gap is seen empty before it fills. Then mark the segment as non-spectral so the seam survives the animation settling — e.g. give the magenta dots a smaller radius or emission-off/wireframe material, or a small plate reading 'no wavelength', so the invented arc stays distinguishable in a still.

findings.claim: Superposition from dipole (two sources cancel/reinforce). Curl from vortex. Convergence from gravity.
findings.mechanism: Superposition is a MAGNITUDE claim, and magnitude is spent on a channel the code has saturated flat. Line 322: `var scale_factor = clampf(magnitude * 0.5, 0.3, 2.0)`. The field is inverse-square (line 281: `r.normalized() * field_strength / (dist * dist + 0.01)`) over a grid of field_size 0.8 / grid_resolution 8 (lines 41,43), so cell centres sit at -0.35..0.35 and every sample is between 0.0707 and 0.495 from the source. That gives POINT_CHARGE magnitudes of 66.7 (nearest) down to 3.92 (corner) — a 17x range — which map to scale 2.0 vs 1.96: a 2% length difference. For DIPOLE (lines 283-295) the net runs from ~60 at the poles down to ~3.85 at the strongest cancellation (perpendicular bisector, x~0.10-0.15, z=+-0.35, where the two z-components annihilate and leave a pure +x residue) → scale 2.0 vs 1.93. The cancel/reinforce structure is quantitatively present in the data and rendered as a 3.5% arrow-length difference: 64 arrows all at the clamp ceiling, all the same length, and at scale 2.0 the arrow spans 0.14 (HEAD_OFFSET 0.06 + head, doubled) against a 0.1 cell pitch, so they interpenetrate into a thicket. Colour, the fastest-read channel, is spent on `alignment` = dot(field, (pos - source_position).normalized()) (lines 326,339) — outward-ness from pole 1 only, which is not the superposition variable; the whole off-axis region reads as one muddy blue→red lerp. The strength slider (lines 220,239 → 0.1 + norm*4.9) is also dead: above field_strength ~1.02 every cell already exceeds the clamp ceiling, so 80% of the slider travel changes only the text on line 377. The vortex half of the claim does read — `profile = dist / (dist * dist + 0.02)` (line 305) yields magnitudes 1.87-3.54 → scales 0.93-1.77, unclamped — which confirms the clamp, not the concept, is what kills the dipole.
findings.fix_sketch: Normalise per update instead of clamping to an absolute ceiling: in `_update_field()` compute the max magnitude over the 64 samples first, then scale each arrow by a compressed ratio (e.g. `lerp(0.3, 1.6, pow(magnitude/max_mag, 0.4))`) so cancellation shows as a visibly short arrow. For DIPOLE, colour by the superposition residue (|F_sum| / (|F1| + |F2|), blue where the two poles cancel, hot where they reinforce) rather than by alignment with pole 1.

findings.claim: the search wavefront's shape reveals the heuristic's bias — Euclidean creates spherical expansion, Manhattan creates diamond-shaped expansion, Chebyshev creates cubic expansion
findings.mechanism: The wavefront never exists. `_ready()` (lines 237-247) builds the grid, obstacles, start and goal, and stops; the only caller of `start_pathfinding()` in the whole repo is line 1027 under `KEY_SPACE` (grep over the tree returns exactly lines 428 and 1027, plus an unrelated file). There is no keyboard in VR, no autostart, no button — so what a visitor stands in front of is permanently static. What that static thing is, per the .tscn overrides (grid_dimensions Vector3i(10,15,10), obstacle_probability 0.2, movement_model 0): a 10 x 15 x 10 metre block of ~300 opaque grey boxes, `material.albedo_color = Color(0.3, 0.3, 0.3)` with no emission (line 392), plus one green start cube and one red goal cube. Nothing ever expands, so no shape is ever produced. Second, the claim is comparative and the comparison has no input path: `heuristic_type` (line 26, default EUCLIDEAN) is never assigned anywhere at runtime — grep shows it only at its declaration, the `match` on line 826, the stats label on line 1004, and the info dict on line 1084. `_input` reaches algorithm_type (KEY_1/2/3), animate_search, show_grid/obstacles/path — never the heuristic. Even on desktop with a keyboard, Euclidean is the only heuristic that can ever be seen, and one wavefront alone reveals no bias. Third, even if it ran, the .tscn sets movement_model 0 (GROUND_BASED) with max_slope_angle 35.0, and `is_movement_allowed` (lines 736-741) rejects every upward step — straight up returns 90 from `calculate_slope_angle`, and even the shallowest corner (1,1,1) is atan(1/1.414) = 35.26 > 35 — so the frontier could only spread sideways and down, never the "spherical expansion" named in the claim. The only place the heuristic is named is the `CanvasLayer` panel built in `setup_ui` (lines 285-302), embedded chrome that is stripped from artifacts placed in maps.
findings.fix_sketch: Call `start_pathfinding()` at the end of `_ready()` and loop it (on finish, `reset_pathfinding()` after a pause) so the wavefront is always mid-expansion when a visitor arrives. Make the comparison co-visible rather than switchable: run two frontiers side by side over the same grid, one MANHATTAN and one EUCLIDEAN, in two tinted overlays, with a Label3D (not the CanvasLayer) naming each. Drop obstacle_probability to ~0.05 and use FLYING for the demo instance so the frontier shape is not dominated by the obstacle field and the no-upward-move constraint.

findings.claim: geometric order from vibration — pattern appears without any particle knowing the whole
findings.mechanism: Three of the ten cycled modes are mathematically dead. `_chladni_amplitude` (line 188) returns `cos(n * x) * cos(m * y) - cos(m * x) * cos(n * y)`, which is identically zero whenever mode_n == mode_m — and `mode_pairs` (lines 51-54) ends with [3, 3], [4, 4], [5, 5]. In those states the force (line 164, `-grad * abs(amplitude) * particle_speed`) is exactly zero, and so is the jitter (line 171, multiplied by `abs(_chladni_amplitude(nx, nz))`), so with `p.velocity * 0.9` damping the sand halts within about half a second. With `auto_cycle_modes = true` and `mode_cycle_time = 8.0` those indices occupy t in [56, 80) of every 80-second loop: 24 seconds in 80, 30% of arrivals, during which the plate visibly keeps buzzing (line 145, `plate.position.y = sin(time * vibration_frequency * TAU * 10) * vibration_amplitude`) while not one particle moves. The visitor sees vibration WITHOUT pattern formation — the exact inverse of the claim — and reads a label (line 201, "Mode (%d, %d)") announcing three different modes over the same frozen leftover [2, 4] figure, which also contradicts the stated critical_parameter that "each pair defines a unique nodal pattern". Secondary, affecting fidelity rather than the verdict: line 164 uses `abs(amplitude)` where descending |A| requires the signed value, since grad(|A|) = sign(A)*grad(A). In negative-amplitude cells the force therefore points away from the nodal lines toward the anti-node centres, so half the figure resolves as blobs at cell centres rather than lines.
findings.fix_sketch: Delete [3, 3], [4, 4], [5, 5] from `mode_pairs` (leaving the seven pairs that produce a field), or guard the cycle with `if mode_m == mode_n: mode_m += 1`, so every labelled mode actually re-sorts the sand. While there, change line 164 to `-grad * amplitude * particle_speed` so both halves of the plate migrate toward the nodal lines.

findings.claim: the visible taxonomy of forces — five simultaneous arrows (gravity, thrust, drag, velocity, acceleration) let you watch how each contributes before they combine
findings.mechanism: A taxonomy needs its members to be tellable apart, and every channel that could do that is either discarded or duplicated. All six arrows share one origin — lines 76-81 assign `ball_pos_scaled` to gravity, thrust, drag, net, velocity and accel every physics frame — so identity can only come from name or colour. The names are never rendered: vector_scene_base.gd:129 does `line_node.set("vector_name", name)`, but lineContainer runs commons/primitives/line/line.gd, which has no such property (grep finds `vector_name` declared only in algorithms/vectors/vectorline/vectorline.gd:17), and Object.set() on an undeclared property is a silent no-op. What line.gd actually draws is its own `length_label` (lines 50-60, 249-262): `length_label.text = "Length: %.2fm" % distance`. So all six co-located arrows carry the same billboarded string — a length in metres, semantically wrong for a force — and no force is ever named. That leaves colour, and three of the six are the same pale blue: gravity Color(0.5, 0.75, 1.0) (line 45), drag Color(0.65, 0.75, 1.0, 0.6) (line 47), velocity Color(0.55, 0.95, 1.0, 0.8) (line 49) — drag differs from gravity by 0.15 in red alone. The alphas the author used to rank them are thrown away too: line.gd:214 sets `material.transparency = BaseMaterial3D.TRANSPARENCY_DISABLED` and line 216 sets `material.emission = line_color`, so drag, net, velocity and accel all render fully opaque and self-lit at full saturation. The one relation the identity block calls out ("the visible drag arrow shows the invisible resistance", drag opposing velocity against gravity) is exactly the trio rendered in one indistinguishable pale blue. Secondary, the taxonomy also leaves the stage within seconds: thrust is a constant (2.5, 0, 0) (line 46), drag gives a terminal 2.5/0.8 = 3.125 logical units/s, and the ground is only 20 x 20 logical (line 157) — about 1.65 m half-extent at SCENE_SCALE 0.33 x root scale 0.5, and invisible, since `_create_ground` builds a StaticBody3D and CollisionShape3D with no mesh — so the ball rolls off in roughly two to three seconds and then falls forever, dragging all six arrows with it via lines 76-81. `_reset_ball()` is bound only to KEY_R (line 120), so a VR visitor arriving any later than that finds an empty plinth and an info panel counting terminal velocity.
findings.fix_sketch: Give each arrow a name in the frame: either add `@export var vector_name` handling to line.gd so `length_label` prints "Gravity |F| = 7.20" (as vectorline.gd:114 already does), or have VectorForces attach its own Label3D at each arrow tip. Re-separate the colours by hue, not alpha, since alpha is discarded — keep gravity blue, move drag to magenta and velocity to white/green. Then fence the ball: bump the ground to a visible platform with lips, or add a bounds check in `_physics_process` that calls `_reset_ball()` when the ball leaves the plinth volume, so the five arrows are on stage when someone walks up.

findings.claim: consonance and dissonance as a visible network — more shared overtones = closer connection
findings.mechanism: Both channels that carry "more shared overtones" are remapped over a domain whose top is unreachable, so the whole network collapses into the bottom 7% of its own designed range. Line 285: `thickness = remap(float(shared), 2.0, 16.0, 0.001, 0.006)`; line 302: `intensity = remap(float(shared), 2.0, 16.0, 0.2, 1.0)`. The top of that domain, shared=16, is `SHARED_OVERTONES[0]` — UNISON (line 72), which cannot occur between two distinct nodes. Worse, lines 238-240 fold the interval: `var interval = absi(idx_j - idx_i)` then `if interval > 6: interval = 12 - interval`, so interval 7 becomes 5 and the entry `7: 5` (line 74) — the perfect fifth, the strongest real consonance in the table — is unreachable dead code; every fifth is scored as a fourth. I enumerated all 66 pairs against the file's own constants: after the `if shared < 2: continue` filter (line 244) exactly 36 lines are drawn and `shared` takes only TWO values — 24 lines at shared=2 and 12 lines at shared=3. That yields cylinder radii 0.00100 m vs 0.00136 m (2.00 mm vs 2.71 mm diameter — a 0.7 mm step) and alphas 0.200 vs 0.257 (a 5.7% step), on a table 0.70 m across (circle_radius 0.35, line 82). The designed maximum (12 mm diameter, alpha 1.0) is never reached by anything. At rest all 12 nodes are also identical DEFAULT_NODE_COLOR = Color(0.85, 0.85, 0.88) (line 67), so the opening state — and every still ever captured — is 12 white spheres inside a uniform faint cyan cobweb where the P5 line and the tritone-adjacent line are visually the same. Then the one channel a viewer reads first gets repurposed on contact: `_update_line_brightness` line 442, `var alpha = 0.8 if connected else 0.15`, so as soon as you touch a node the alpha stops encoding `shared` at all and becomes binary connected/not — every line from the tonal centre gets alpha 0.8 whether it shares 3 overtones or 2, leaving only the 0.7 mm thickness step to carry the entire claim. The ranking is correct (the 12 shared=3 lines are exactly the circle-of-fifths adjacencies); the visual magnitude of the difference is not renderable.
findings.fix_sketch: Remap over the reachable range, not the theoretical one. Drop the `interval > 6` fold (or key SHARED_OVERTONES by directed semitone distance) so interval 7 keeps its 5, then use `remap(shared, 2.0, 5.0, 0.0015, 0.006)` for thickness and `remap(shared, 2.0, 5.0, 0.30, 1.0)` for alpha — the fifth then renders at 12 mm/α1.0 against the weak connections' 3 mm/α0.30. In `_update_line_brightness`, keep the shared-proportional alpha as the base and express connected/not on a second channel (emission_energy or hue desaturation) so touching a node never flattens the variable the claim is about.

findings.claim: landscape-like patterns without a landscape designer — rivers, shores, and paths appear because ecology IS a local-constraint system; the algorithm finds the same shapes biology does
findings.mechanism: I ported `_solve_wfc`/`_attempt_solve`/`_propagate`/`_is_compatible`/`_backtrack` verbatim (including the 10-attempt retry and the 200-deep history slice) and ran 20 solves at grid_size 16. None of the three named features appears. Mean tile share of the 256 cells: SAND 38.3%, WATER 28.0%, PATH 14.3%, GROUND 12.8%, GRASS 3.2% (min 0), STONE 3.3% (min 0) — two of the six terrain types are effectively extinct and sometimes literally absent. Mean 4-connected region size is 2.75 cells and mean neighbour-match fraction is 0.364 (a coherent landscape runs ~0.85); a typical panel has 74-130 separate regions in 256 cells. So no rivers (water arrives as 1-22 cell specks, or in one trial a single 58-cell lake covering 23% of the panel), and no paths (largest PATH region 4-11 cells, most are 1-3 cell specks). Two source lines cause it. Line 188: `var chosen: int = opts[_rng.randi() % opts.size()]` — uniform, despite the comment on line 187 saying "pick a weighted random tile"; there is no frequency table anywhere in the file, so nothing biases toward contiguity. Line 61: `Tile.SAND: [Tile.SAND, Tile.WATER, Tile.GROUND, Tile.PATH]` omits GRASS and STONE, and SAND is the ONLY tile WATER may touch (line 60, `[Tile.WATER, Tile.SAND]`) — so sand+water self-reinforce to 66% of the grid and `_propagate` then prunes GRASS and STONE out of every cell adjacent to that 38%. The constraint isn't producing ecology; it is squeezing four of six terrains to the margin, and nothing on the panel says so. Second, the margin is actively disguised: 3 of my 20 runs exhausted all 10 attempts and hit `return _fallback_grid()` (line 122), which is a hard-coded `((x + y) % 2) * 3` GROUND/GRASS checkerboard (lines 311-318) — passed straight into `_render_grid` with no marking, so 15% of placements show the one pattern WFC could never produce, presented as a WFC solve. All entropy, propagation and backtracking happen inside a single `_ready()` frame (line 79) and are never drawn; there is no adjacency legend, no contradiction cell, no remaining-options count. Rendering compounds it: 0.8 m panel / 16 tiles = 5 cm pitch at 4 px per tile, and the grid lines at `g * pixel_scale` (lines 342-351) darken 1 of every 4 pixel rows, so the lattice occupies 25% of each tile's width while the largest coherent feature is ~12 cm.
findings.fix_sketch: Two changes. (1) Make coherence reachable: add a frequency-weighted pick at line 188 and let SAND neighbour GRASS/STONE (line 61) so a 38%-of-grid tile stops pruning them out — target mean 4-connected region size ≥8 rather than 2.75, verified by the same harness before shipping. (2) Stop hiding the fence: never render `_fallback_grid()` as a solve — leave failed cells uncollapsed and colour them by remaining-option count, keep the contradiction cell visible, and bake a small adjacency strip onto the panel edge ("water ↮ stone") so the constraint that shapes the field is on the floor next to its output.

findings.claim: the four-knob radar makes the formula's STATE legible at a glance — F top, E right, λ bottom, φ left, polygon shape tells you which phase the system is in before you read the readout; QFE sign tells you whether order or entropy wins; the halo color says where on the spine you are
findings.mechanism: The axis mapping is exactly right (lines 452-455: top = radar_max·F, right = radar_max·E, bottom = −radar_max·λ, left = −radar_max·φ, with matching-colour axis tags at 356-359), the sign prints (`%+.2f`, line 705), and the halo retints (line 656). What fails is the clause "polygon shape tells you which phase the system is in" — and the reason is that `_detect_phase()` (lines 257-268) is an unthresholded argmin whose fit distance is computed into `best_d` at lines 265-266 and then thrown away. Measuring the hard-coded PHASE_DATA signatures (lines 79-136) at radar_max = 0.42: oscillation (.65/.55/.40/.30) and lambda_edge (.55/.58/.40/.35) are Manhattan 0.18 apart, which on the radar is a 4.2 cm difference at top, 1.3 cm at right, 0.0 cm at bottom and 2.1 cm at left — on a 42 cm radar. lambda_edge vs relation is 0.43, integration vs synthesis 0.38. Sampling 200k points of [0,1]⁴, those four crowded signatures claim ~70% of the operating space (relation 21.1%, integration 18.8%, lambda_edge 17.7%, oscillation 12.1%), so over most of the knob range the quadrilateral cannot discriminate the phase and the reading actually comes from the colour — a downstream product of the classifier, not of the shape. Because best_d is discarded, the instrument asserts a phase with identical visual confidence at every fit quality: the worst sampled point (F=0.00, E=0.02, λ=0.01, φ=0.96) is Manhattan 1.77 from "relation" and still gets the yellow halo, the letter G and the flat text `"dominant phase: %s"` (line 564). Turn all four knobs to zero and the console reports "F — Order", blue halo, letter F, formula "QFE ≈ F" — the ORDER phase, at fit distance 1.05, with QFE = 0.00 and a polygon collapsed to a single point at the hub. That is the margin, and the @identity's own relationships line names it ("the knobs sit BETWEEN regions, never inside one of them") while nothing on the instrument renders betweenness: `_phase_index` is always one of 0..6 and there is no not-in-a-region state.
findings.fix_sketch: Surface the number `_detect_phase` already computes. Return `best_d` alongside the index and (a) drive confidence off it — lerp the phase colour toward neutral grey and drop `_halo_material.emission_energy_multiplier` as best_d grows past ~0.35, so a bad fit looks like a bad fit; (b) append `"fit: %.2f"` to the readout lines next to `dominant phase`; and (c) draw the nearest signature's quadrilateral as a dim ghost outline behind the live one in `_refresh_radar`, so the shape→phase comparison the claim promises happens on screen instead of in the classifier.

findings.claim: the specimen-as-meditation — continuous rotation reveals what static display cannot
findings.mechanism: The rotation exists, is continuous, and the axis choice is the one that actually discloses helicity. Line 85 `helix.rotation.y += delta * rotation_speed` (0.2 rad/s) stacks with the child's own `auto_rotate = true` / `rotation_speed = 0.3` and `rotate_y(rotation_speed * delta)` (doublehelix.gd lines 106-107, 133), giving ~0.5 rad/s ≈ 12.6 s per revolution — slow enough for the meditation framing. Rotating about Y is the helix's screw axis: with positions_a[i] = (cos(i·Δθ)·r, y0 + i·Δy, sin(i·Δθ)·r) (doublehelix.gd line 188), a rotation by α maps the point set onto itself translated vertically, so the two strands read as a barber pole — apparent vertical travel plus which colour crosses in front, which is exactly the pitch-and-handedness information a still frame cannot give. The two strands stay distinguishable: helix_color_a Color(0.2, 0.6, 1.0) and helix_color_b Color(1.0, 0.4, 0.6) (lines 22-23) are pushed into the child at lines 75-76 before the deferred `_rebuild` fires (child `_ready` queues, parent `_ready` sets, one rebuild runs with the new values), and `_create_strand` only lerps instance colour toward white by ≤0.25 (doublehelix.gd line 225), preserving hue — no grey-emission flattening of the kind that broke basis_vectors_rig. Scale and occlusion check out: HelixContainer scale 0.15 × helix_radius 0.5 = 0.075 m world radius inside a fluid cylinder of radius 0.11 spanning y 0.05–0.43, helix spanning y 0.125–0.425, so it sits inside the fluid; front-face transmission is (1−0.12)·(1−0.30) ≈ 0.62 through jar and fluid (lines 46, 24) with the strands emissive at glow 1.5, and the fluid's pulsed emission only adds ≤0.12 in green (lines 89-90). Two sub-threshold notes, not findings: the rungs and axis beam use PRIMITIVE_LINES / LINE_STRIP (doublehelix.gd lines 242, 284) so they render as 1-pixel hairlines at 0.15 scale, making the base pairs named in the truth line the least visible part of the specimen; and `rotation_speed`, declared the critical_parameter, cannot stop the spin — setting it to 0 via apply_grid_config still leaves the child's independent 0.3 rad/s.

findings.claim: same script, four signs — green EXIT →, red EMERGENCY ↓, phase-tinted λ-S LAB ←, contextual RETURN ↑
findings.mechanism: Colour is spent on the variable that carries the claim. `_build_body()` sets BOTH `mat.albedo_color = sign_color` (113) and `mat.emission = sign_color` (115) at `emission_energy_multiplier = glow_energy` (1.5) — no grey-out (contrast basis_vectors_rig's uniform Color(0.5,0.5,0.5)) and no alpha-scaling bug. The text does not cover the colour: `BakedTextAlbedo.generate_text_image` fills the image `Color(0,0,0,0)` (line 61) and writes only glyph coverage, and `_text_quad` sets TRANSPARENCY_ALPHA, so the sign_color body reads around and behind white letters. The per-placement variation is real, not hypothetical: Trial_doors_gate carries 8 tokens with three distinct colours — `exit_sign:90:2.0#text:THRESHOLD#sign_color:0.20,0.80,0.30` (green egress), `exit_sign:270:2.0#text:QUARANTINE#sign_color:0.85,0.20,0.18` (red warning), and six phase-tinted blue `#sign_color:0.35,0.60,0.95` lab names (HELICOID, GEODESIC DOME, CSG DIFFERENCE D, …). The plumbing works: GridInteractablesComponent parses `#key:value` (line 876) and calls `apply_grid_config` deferred (1575), which sets `config_*` meta, and `_parse_color` (190–200) correctly reads the comma triple; `_clear_built_children` + rebuild means the override actually takes. Legibility: `_fit_font_size` yields ~58px of a 139px-tall image for a 16-char name on the 0.45×0.18 m face, i.e. ~3 cm cap height on a sign mounted at y_offset 2.0 — normal exit-sign proportion for a lab room. One honest gap, not a code defect: `arrow_direction` defaults to "none" (28) and `_build_arrow()` returns at 158–159 on "none", and not one of the 13 placement tokens across Trial_doors_gate and Trial_span_br sets it — so no sign in the project actually points at anything. The colour-and-text half of the claim renders; the four arrow glyphs have no instance in the field even though the mechanism exists and works.

findings.claim: locomotion as a vector sum — the chevrons + the glowing arrow show the exact direction you'll fly before you commit your feet
findings.mechanism: The chevrons point 180° away from the launch. Line 86: `chev.rotation_degrees = Vector3(-90, 0, 0)   # point +Z, lying flat`. A CylinderMesh with `top_radius = 0.0` (84) has its apex at local +Y; R_x(−90°) maps (0,1,0) → (0, cos(−90), sin(−90)) = (0,0,−1) = **−Z**. But the launch is toward +Z: `_launch_velocity()` line 115 reads `var fwd := global_transform.basis.z   # pad forward (+Z)` and returns `fwd.normalized() * forward_force + Vector3.UP * up_force`. Verified against this codebase's own convention rather than from memory: pattern_loom.gd:611, pattern_machine_c.gd:410 and hangar_kit.gd:261 all use `Vector3(90, 0, 0)` commented "faces +Z", and fuzzy_cloud.gd:342 uses `Vector3(-90,0,0)` for "Point downward" (spotlight −Z → −Y) — both confirm the sign. So the three chevrons, the pad's loudest directional cue and the thing a player reads before stepping on, aim backward. The brightness ramp agrees with the wrong direction too: `emission_energy_multiplier = 2.8 - i * 0.5` paired with `position = Vector3(0, 0.15, -0.28 + i * 0.26)` (87, 91) makes the −Z chevron brightest (2.8) and the +Z one dimmest (1.8), so the flow gradient also points −Z. The single placement token is `force_pad:0:0` (rotation 0), so nothing cancels the error. Meanwhile the arrow — which `_refresh_arrow` computes correctly as local (0, 0.759, 0.651) via `global_transform.basis.inverse() * dir`, making it yaw-independent — points the opposite way from the chevrons. The two halves of the claim's own evidence contradict each other, and the flat floor chevrons are the half a player reads first. Compounding: `_position_arrow` line 206 sets `arrow.basis = Basis(b.x, dir, -b.z)` where `b := Basis.looking_at(dir, up)` gives `b.z = -dir`, so `-b.z == dir` — the Y and Z columns are the same vector, a singular basis (det 0) that collapses the 0.03-radius shaft and 0.09-radius head into a zero-thickness blade, and `_make_arrow`'s material sets UNSHADED but never `cull_mode = CULL_DISABLED`, so the arrow vanishes edge-on when approached from ±X.
findings.fix_sketch: Line 86 → `chev.rotation_degrees = Vector3(90, 0, 0)` and invert the brightness ramp to `2.8 - (2 - i) * 0.5` so the brightest chevron sits at the +Z tip. Line 206 → build an orthonormal basis, e.g. `arrow.basis = Basis(b.x, dir, b.x.cross(dir))`, and add `mat.cull_mode = BaseMaterial3D.CULL_DISABLED` in `_make_arrow`.

findings.claim: creatures converge on similar body plans despite random initialization — convergent evolution from pure math
findings.mechanism: The artifact shows generation 0 — the maximally NON-converged state — and there is no path to advance it inside a map, so the claimed phenomenon never occurs. Three locks, all in source: (1) `@export var auto_evolve: bool = false` (42) and `_process` (146–151) steps only when it is true; the .tscn sets no override. (2) The two advance controls are editor-only export setters — `evolve_one_generation` (44–48) and `reset_evolution` (49–53) — and the in-scene UI that could drive them (GeneticProgramming.tscn `AutoCheck` CheckBox, unchecked, and `EvolveButton`) lives under a `CanvasLayer`, which `GridInteractablesComponent._suppress_embedded_chrome` sets `visible = false` on for every placed artifact (1002–1010, invoked at 1187 and again deferred at 1188). (3) `func apply_grid_config(config: Dictionary) -> void: pass` (746–747) discards all map config, so no placement token can switch `auto_evolve` on — the token that exists, `GeneticProgramming#with_wall:true#with_pillars:true#with_barrier:true`, is silently dropped. Net: `_ready()` → `initialize_population()` builds 20 genomes of `randi() % genome_complexity + 3` genes each with `randf_range` position/rotation/scale (117–133), calls `visualize_population()` once, and freezes. A visitor sees 20 random blobs for the entire visit; every still ever captured is generation 0. Same failure shape as monte_carlo_dartboard's blank board, except here there is no rate to wait out. Supporting: `fitness_history.append(best_genome.fitness)` (264) accumulates the one quantity that would show convergence and is never rendered anywhere; the only readout is `Label3D` at `font_size = 16` on a grid of `spacing = 6.0` m cells (724–728); and every phenotype gets the same constant `material.albedo_color = Color(0.6, 0.7, 0.9)` (486), so colour distinguishes neither fitness nor generation.
findings.fix_sketch: Pre-seed the accumulation, the dartboard fix: in `initialize_population`, after the first `evaluate_population()`, run `for _i in range(25): evolve_generation()` before the first `visualize_population()`, so a visitor arrives at a converged population and can still watch it move. Then default `auto_evolve = true`, and replace `apply_grid_config`'s `pass` with reads of `auto_evolve`, `fitness_function` and `mutation_rate` so placements can pick the selection pressure. Render `fitness_history` as a row of bars beside the grid so the convergence has a visible trace.

findings.claim: Rain streaking diagonally as the decomposition display shows wind + gravity = trajectory
findings.mechanism: The rain half reads: `_drive_rain` writes `_rain_mat.gravity = (grav_term + wind_term) * sc` (1551–1554) and the streak quad uses `billboard_mode = BILLBOARD_PARTICLES` (651), so the geometry genuinely tilts to the resultant. The decomposition display half does not read, for three reasons in source. (a) The two gains disagree by ~29×: `_drive_rain` uses `grav_term = (0, -gravity_strength * 9.8, 0)` and `wind_term = Vector3(sum.x, 0, sum.z) * 3.0`, while `_update_decomposition` (1636–1638) uses `wind_vec = sum` and `grav_vec = (0, -gravity_strength, 0)`. In Storm mode (MODE_VECTORS_A[2] + MODE_VECTORS_B[2] = (3.0, 0, 2.2), gravity_strength 1.0) the rain falls 41° below horizontal while the display's orange 'trajectory' rod sits 15° below horizontal — the display draws a 26°-different slant from the thing its own label captions. (b) The rods collapse. `_orient_decomp_arrow` line 1655: `arrow_len = clampf(mag * 0.2, 0.03, 0.4) * sc`; in Storm the wind rod (mag 3.72) and the result rod (mag 3.85) both saturate the 0.4 clamp, so they are the same length and only 15° apart from a shared origin — and `_create_decomp_arrow` (1138–1152) builds a bare `CylinderMesh` with `top_radius = bottom_radius = 0.008` and no head cone at all, unlike the field arrows which get `_arrow_head_mm`. Three undirected 8 mm rods (0.004 m radius after the root `scale = Vector3(0.5,0.5,0.5)`), two of them near-coincident, radiating from one point rather than chained head-to-tail, cannot be read as 'A + B = C'. (c) Placement washes it out: `decomp_root.position = Vector3(domain_extent*0.7, 0.3, domain_extent*0.7) * sc` puts it at world ≈ (1.75, 0.25, 1.75) — a far corner of the ~5 m chamber, 25 cm off the floor, inside the ground-mist emitter (`_mist_gpu.position = (0, 0.1, 0) * sc`, `slab.size = Vector2(1.2,1.2) * sc`, `scale_min 1.8`/`scale_max 3.2`, additive) and competing with 144 field arrows at `emission_energy_multiplier = 2.0` and 460 additive rain streaks at 2.2. Its only caption is `decomp_label.font_size = 14` at alpha 0.8, and `_update_info_text` (1916–1920) prints A, B, A+B and heading but never gravity or slant, so no numeric readout backs it up. Also a colour collision: `decomp_wind_arrow = _create_decomp_arrow(Color(0.3, 0.85, 0.95))` (1116) is exactly `wind_a`'s cyan (458) yet carries `wind_vec = sum` (1636) — whose colour everywhere else in the chamber is the resultant's yellow `Color(1.0, 0.9, 0.2)` (474). The display paints the sum in the colour the artifact has spent the whole room teaching you means 'component A'. (Secondary, on the D2 axis: `_build_all` ends with `_apply_mode(0)` = Calm, wind (0.3, 0.05, 0), so the opening rain slant is ~5° from vertical — 'diagonal' needs two MODE presses.)
findings.fix_sketch: Make `_update_decomposition` use the rain's own terms — `grav_vec = (0, -gravity_strength * 9.8, 0)`, `wind_vec = Vector3(sum.x, 0, sum.z) * 3.0` — then divide all three by the resultant's magnitude and multiply by one fixed display length, so the drawn angle equals the rain's angle and the clamp stops eating it. Chain them head-to-tail (wind from the origin, gravity from wind's tip, result origin→tip) and give each a head cone like `_arrow_head_mm`. Recolour the wind rod to the resultant yellow, or split it into cyan A + magenta B so the colour code stays honest. Raise `decomp_root` to chest height (y ≈ 1.4 m) out of the mist and off the corner.

findings.claim: The ghost arrow -B appearing at A's tip makes the tip-to-tail construction visible
findings.mechanism: C:\Users\palle\Documents\GitHub\AdaResearch_46\commons\artifacts\vector_subtraction_demo\vector_subtraction_demo.gd — `_position_arrow` (lines 442-464) never assigns `arrow.position`. The arrow Node3D stays at the artifact origin while lines 463-464 rotate it (`arrow.look_at(arrow.global_position + direction, up)` then `rotate_object_local(Vector3.RIGHT, PI/2)`), and its children hold PARENT-space offsets computed at lines 455-457 (`shaft.position = mid`, `head.position = end - direction.normalized() * arrow_thickness * 2.5`). Those offsets are therefore re-expressed through the rotated basis, so every arrow is drawn correctly-shaped but rigidly rotated about the origin, away from the vector it represents. Replicating Godot's `Basis.looking_at` + `rotate_object_local(RIGHT, PI/2)` on the defaults A=(0.8,0.4,-0.1), B=(0.2,0.7,0.3): arrow A's shaft midpoint is intended at (0.4,0.2,-0.05) and renders at (-0.15,-0.044,0.422); its head is intended at (0.787,0.393,-0.098) and renders at (-0.295,-0.087,0.830). It neither starts at A's tip (0.8,0.4,-0.1) nor lands on A-B=(0.6,-0.3,-0.4): the construction triangle never closes. Local +Y also maps to -direction, so each cone head points back down its own shaft. The labels are separate children of `self` (lines 431-434, `_label_a.position = vector_a * 0.5 + ...`) and are never rotated, so 'A', 'B', '-B', 'A-B' float at the CORRECT midpoints with rods scattered nowhere near them; the coordinate axes are built by a different, correct path (`_create_axis_line`, lines 218-239, sets `shaft.position` on a childless node) so the axes are right while the vectors are wrong, making the mismatch conspicuous. findings.fix_sketch: Port adder_board.gd:780-807 over `_position_arrow` (lines 442-464): build the basis with y_axis = dir/length, set `arrow.transform = Transform3D(Basis(x_axis,y_axis,z_axis), start)`, place children at local +Y only (`shaft.position = Vector3(0, shaft_len*0.5, 0)`, `head.position = Vector3(0, length - arrow_thickness*2.5, 0)`), and delete the look_at + rotate_object_local pair. findings.claim: The relationship between the three vectors becomes legible — velocity always tangent to the trail, acceleration always bending it — without any formula on screen
findings.mechanism: C:\Users\palle\Documents\GitHub\AdaResearch_46\algorithms\vectors\08_vector_motion\VectorMotion.gd — motion is the whole subject, and the bend of the path is driven by a force the artifact never draws. `create_ball` (shared base, algorithms\vectors\shared\vector_scene_base.gd:417-456) never sets `gravity_scale`, and project.godot has no gravity override, so Godot's default 9.8 m/s^2 down is live. Line 86 applies only `accel_logical * ball.mass * SCENE_SCALE` = (1.5,0.5,0) * 1.0 * 0.33 = 0.165 m/s^2 in y — 59x weaker than gravity and opposite in sign.
